The identification of a correct order parameter (and corresponding pure-state / metastate structure) for finite-dimensional short-range spin glasses remains one of the central unresolved problems in the rigorous and physical theory of disordered systems. Consider a Bayesian cooperative game with transferable utility defined as follows. A finite set N of players is given. Each player i ∈ N has a finite type space T_i; let T = ∏_{i∈N} T_i. A prior probability distribution p on T is given, and the basic game G specifies, for each coalition S ⊆ N, each profile of actions, and each type profile, a transferable monetary payoff. Under the independent private values (IPV) assumption, p is a product distribution p = ∏_i p_i on T, and each player's von Neumann–Morgenstern utility depends only on actions and on his own type. Under the ex ante coalition-commitment assumption, coalitions form and commit to (incentive-compatible, state-contingent) cooperative agreements before players learn their types.

Under these two assumptions (IPV and ex ante commitment), a body of results characterizes various notions of the core (ex ante, interim, coarse, fine, etc.) for such Bayesian TU games, including non-emptiness theorems, balancedness conditions, and equivalence results.

Problem. Extend these core-based results to Bayesian TU games in which (a) the independent private values assumption is dropped, allowing correlated types and/or common-value components; (b) the ex ante coalition-commitment assumption is dropped, allowing coalitions to form at the interim stage (after players learn their types) rather than at the ex ante stage; or (c) both assumptions are simultaneously dropped. Specifically, formulate appropriate notions of the core in each of these relaxed settings and establish corresponding existence (non-emptiness), characterization, and equivalence theorems analogous to the IPV/ex-ante-commitment case.

Consider a Bayesian cooperative game with transferable utility defined as follows. A finite set N of players is given. Each player i ∈ N has a finite type space T_i; let T = ∏_{i∈N} T_i. A prior probability distribution p on T is given, and the basic game G specifies, for each coalition S ⊆ N, each profile of actions, and each type profile, a transferable monetary payoff. Under the independent private values (IPV) assumption, p is a product distribution p = ∏_i p_i on T, and each player's von Neumann–Morgenstern utility depends only on actions and on his own type. Under the ex ante coalition-commitment assumption, coalitions form and commit to (incentive-compatible, state-contingent) cooperative agreements before players learn their types.

Under these two assumptions (IPV and ex ante commitment), a body of results characterizes various notions of the core (ex ante, interim, coarse, fine, etc.) for such Bayesian TU games, including non-emptiness theorems, balancedness conditions, and equivalence results.

Problem. Extend these core-based results to Bayesian TU games in which (a) the independent private values assumption is dropped, allowing correlated types and/or common-value components; (b) the ex ante coalition-commitment assumption is dropped, allowing coalitions to form at the interim stage (after players learn their types) rather than at the ex ante stage; or (c) both assumptions are simultaneously dropped. Specifically, formulate appropriate notions of the core in each of these relaxed settings and establish corresponding existence (non-emptiness), characterization, and equivalence theorems analogous to the IPV/ex-ante-commitment case.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The literature on Bayesian cooperative TU games (e.g., Forges–Minelli–Vohra, Myerson's virtual-utility core, Forges–Serrano surveys) treats relaxation of independent private values and of ex ante commitment as an active and largely unresolved research direction. Partial progress exists for specific solution concepts (e.g., interim core variants, virtual-utility cores, NTU extensions) but no comprehensive extension of the core-based results to non-IPV and/or non-ex-ante-commitment settings has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

Informal setup. Consider subsets X ⊆ ℕ. For such a set, formulate the following five conditions, where the words "known" and "naturally defined" refer to the present state of mathematical knowledge:

(1) There is a known algorithm that, with no input, returns an integer n such that, if X is finite, then every element of X is ≤ n.
(2) There is a known algorithm that, for every k ∈ ℕ, decides whether k ∈ X.
(3) No currently known algorithm with no input returns the truth value of the statement "X is infinite."
(4) Many elements of X are known, and it is conjectured but not yet proved that X is infinite.
(5) X is naturally defined; the statement that X is infinite is either false or unproven; and among all currently known sets Y ⊆ ℕ that have the same set of currently known elements as X, the set X admits the simplest definition.

Question. Does there exist a decidable set X ⊆ ℕ for which Conditions (1)–(5) all hold simultaneously?

Let $R = \bigoplus_{i\ge 0} R_i$ be a graded $k$-algebra with $R_0 = k$ a field and $R$ generated in degree $1$, with graded maximal ideal $\mathfrak m = \bigoplus_{i\ge 1} R_i$. Let
$$\cdots \to F_2 \to F_1 \to F_0 \to k \to 0$$
be the minimal graded free resolution of the residue field $k = R/\mathfrak m$ over $R$, and write $t_i^R(k) = \sup\{\, j : (F_i)_j \neq 0\,\}$ for the maximal degree of a generator of $F_i$ (equivalently the top nonzero degree in $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(k,k)$). The rate of $R$ is defined as
$$\operatorname{rate}(R) = \sup_{i \ge 2} \frac{t_i^R(k) - 1}{i - 1}.$$
One always has $\operatorname{rate}(R) \ge \operatorname{reg}\nolimits_R(k)$-type bounds, and $\operatorname{rate}(R) = 1$ if and only if $R$ is Koszul.

Problem. Identify natural classes of standard graded $k$-algebras $R$ for which a sharp upper bound on $\operatorname{rate}(R)$ can be established in terms of natural invariants of $R$ (such as the degrees of a minimal generating set of the defining ideal, the regularity of $R$, or combinatorial data when $R$ is defined by monomial or toric relations), and prove that the bound is sharp by exhibiting rings attaining it.

Consider an Edwards–Anderson short-range spin glass on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ ($d$ finite, e.g. $d=3$) with Hamiltonian
$$H(\sigma) = -\sum_{\langle x,y\rangle} J_{xy}\,\sigma_x \sigma_y, \qquad \sigma_x \in \{-1,+1\},$$
where the couplings $J_{xy}$ on nearest-neighbor bonds are i.i.d. random variables drawn from a symmetric distribution (e.g. Gaussian or $\pm 1$). Equip the spin configuration space with a stochastic single-spin-flip dynamics (e.g. heat-bath or Glauber dynamics) at inverse temperature $\beta$ in the putative spin-glass phase, started from a random initial configuration at "waiting time" $t_w = 0$.

Define the two-time autocorrelation
$$C(t_w + t,\, t_w) \;=\; \frac{1}{|\Lambda|}\sum_{x \in \Lambda} \mathbb{E}\!\left[\sigma_x(t_w+t)\,\sigma_x(t_w)\right],$$
where the expectation is over the dynamics and the disorder. Experimentally and numerically, $C(t_w + t, t_w)$ exhibits aging: for large $t_w$ it is not a function of $t$ alone but depends nontrivially on the ratio (or some scaling combination) of $t$ and $t_w$, and the system never reaches equilibrium on accessible time scales.

Problem. Develop a rigorous theoretical framework for the long-time, non-equilibrium dynamics of finite-dimensional short-range spin glasses that:
(i) derives, from the microscopic Hamiltonian above, the asymptotic form of $C(t_w+t,t_w)$ and of the associated response function $R(t_w+t,t_w)$ in the aging regime;
(ii) explains the observed violation of the fluctuation–dissipation theorem and identifies the corresponding effective temperature(s);
(iii) provides operational criteria, applicable to laboratory and simulated systems with slow relaxation, for deciding whether the system is effectively in or out of equilibrium on a given observational time window.

Let $k$ be a field and let $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be a polynomial ring equipped with a monomial order $\prec$. For an ideal $I \subset S$, the initial ideal $\operatorname{in}_\prec(I)$ is the monomial ideal generated by the leading monomials (with respect to $\prec$) of all elements of $I$. A Gröbner basis of $I$ with respect to $\prec$ is a finite subset $G \subset I$ whose leading monomials generate $\operatorname{in}_\prec(I)$. A Gröbner basis $G$ is called quadratic if every element of $G$ has degree at most $2$, equivalently if $\operatorname{in}_\prec(I)$ is generated by monomials of degree at most $2$. An ideal $I$ is said to have a quadratic Gröbner basis if there exists some choice of coordinates and some monomial order with respect to which $I$ admits a quadratic Gröbner basis. It is known that ideals with a quadratic Gröbner basis are Koszul, but the converse fails in general.

Problem. Identify and describe broad classes of homogeneous ideals $I \subset S$ that possess a quadratic Gröbner basis. In particular, give structural or combinatorial criteria on $I$ (or on the algebra $S/I$) that guarantee the existence of coordinates and a monomial order under which $I$ has a Gröbner basis consisting of polynomials of degree at most $2$.

Let $\mathbb{N}$ denote the natural numbers. An indexed family of languages is a sequence $(L_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ together with a total recursive function $f : \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \{0,1\}$ such that $f(i,x) = 1$ iff $x \in L_i$.

An informant for a language $L \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is an infinite sequence enumerating every pair $(x, \chi_L(x))$ for $x \in \mathbb{N}$, where $\chi_L$ is the characteristic function of $L$. A learner $M$ is a (possibly partial) computable function that, given a finite initial segment of an informant, outputs an index (in some hypothesis space, i.e., an effective numbering of languages). $M$ identifies $L$ in the limit from informants if, on every informant for $L$, the sequence of conjectured indices converges to a single index that denotes $L$.

The learner $M$ is strongly monotonic if, for every informant and any two stages $n < m$, the language denoted by its conjecture at stage $n$ is a subset of the language denoted by its conjecture at stage $m$. The learner is iterative if there is a computable function $F$ and an initial conjecture $h_0$ such that the conjecture at stage $n+1$ depends only on the previous conjecture $h_n$ and the next datum from the informant: $h_{n+1} = F(h_n, d_{n+1})$.

A hypothesis space $(H_j)_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ used by a learner for an indexed family $(L_i)$ is called class-preserving if every $H_j$ equals some $L_i$.

Question: Does there exist an indexed family $(L_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ such that
(a) $(L_i)$ is strongly monotonically identifiable in the limit from informants by some algorithmic learner (using a class-preserving hypothesis space), yet
(b) $(L_i)$ is not strongly monotonically identifiable in the limit from informants by any iterative learner, regardless of the hypothesis space the iterative learner is permitted to use?

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The question, originally posed by Lange and Zeugmann, has been answered affirmatively: there exists an indexed family which is strongly monotonically identifiable from informant by a learner using a class-preserving hypothesis space, but not by any iterative learner even with an arbitrary hypothesis space. This separation is established in recent work on incremental learning in the limit from positive and negative information.

Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^N$ be a smooth projective toric variety that is projectively normal in its given embedding. Equivalently, let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a smooth lattice polytope (i.e., a lattice polytope at each of whose vertices the primitive edge vectors form a basis of $\mathbb{Z}^n$) such that for every positive integer $k$, every lattice point of $kP$ is a sum of $k$ lattice points of $P$ (so the associated projective toric variety $X_P$ is projectively normal). Let $I_P \subset k[x_a : a \in P \cap \mathbb{Z}^n]$ denote the toric ideal defining $X_P$, that is, the kernel of the ring homomorphism sending $x_a$ to $t^a \cdot s$ in the polynomial ring $k[t_1^{\pm 1},\dots,t_n^{\pm 1},s]$.

Prove or disprove: the ideal $I_P$ is generated by quadratic binomials.

representations.normalized:
Consider the autonomous Nicholson blowflies delay differential equation
  N'(t) = P N(t-s) exp(-N(t-s)) - d N(t),
where P, d > 0 are constants with P > d and s > 0 is a constant maturation delay; this equation has the unique positive equilibrium N* = ln(P/d).

Consider the following three nonautonomous generalizations on t ≥ 0, in which h(t) is a measurable delay function satisfying t - s ≤ h(t) ≤ t for some s > 0, R(t,·) is, for each t, a nondecreasing function of bounded variation with R(t,t) - R(t,h(t)) = 1, the coefficients a_k(t) ≥ 0 satisfy Σ_{k=1}^m a_k(t) ≡ 1, the delays h_k(t) satisfy t - s ≤ h_k(t) ≤ t, and K(t,u) ≥ 0 with ∫_{h(t)}^{t} K(t,u) du = 1:

 (A) Distributed-delay model:
     N'(t) = -d N(t) + P ∫_{h(t)}^{t} N(u) exp(-N(u)) d_u R(t,u).

 (B) Multiple-delay model:
     N'(t) = -d N(t) + P Σ_{k=1}^m a_k(t) N(h_k(t)) exp(-N(h_k(t))).

 (C) Integro-differential model:
     N'(t) = -d N(t) + P ∫_{h(t)}^{t} K(t,u) N(u) exp(-N(u)) du.

Each of (A), (B), (C) admits N* = ln(P/d) as a positive equilibrium when P > d.

Solve the following:
 (i) Establish sufficient global stability criteria for the positive equilibrium N* of each of (A), (B), (C) whose strength matches the best known sufficient criteria available for the autonomous equation.
 (ii) Determine whether the best known sufficient global stability criteria for the autonomous equation remain valid when the constant delay s is replaced by an arbitrary variable delay h(t) with t - s ≤ h(t) ≤ t.
 (iii) Find necessary delay-dependent conditions for global stability of the positive equilibrium for both the autonomous equation and for each of the nonautonomous models (A), (B), (C).

Recent literature on nonautonomous Nicholson blowflies models reports progress only on delay-independent global stability criteria (via fluctuation lemma and differential inequalities), while sharp delay-dependent and necessary conditions matching the strongest known autonomous results remain unresolved. Let $\mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. For a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, call an integer $n$ a threshold number of $X$ if the following implication holds:
$$\operatorname{card}(X) < \omega \;\Longrightarrow\; X \subseteq (-\infty, n].$$
(Equivalently, $n$ is a threshold number of $X$ provided that whenever $X$ is finite, every element of $X$ is at most $n$; if $X$ is infinite, the condition is vacuously satisfied.)

Let $T = \{p \in \mathbb{N} : p \text{ and } p+2 \text{ are both prime}\}$ be the set of twin primes (the smaller member of each twin prime pair). Determine whether there is currently a known explicit integer $n$ that can be proved to be a threshold number of $T$; that is, exhibit such an $n$ together with a proof that if $T$ is finite then $\max T \le n$, or show that no such explicit $n$ is presently known.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

No explicit known threshold number for the set of twin primes appears in the literature. Knowing such an integer would be equivalent to knowing an a priori bound beyond which finiteness of the twin prime set would be ruled out, which is closely tied to the unresolved twin prime conjecture. Related work (e.g., Tyszka's hypothetical statements implying the existence of a computable threshold for the twin primes) is conditional and does not exhibit such an integer. The problem is therefore considered open.

Let $k$ be an infinite field, let $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be a standard graded polynomial ring, and fix positive integers $d_1, \dots, d_m$. Consider an ideal $I = (f_1, \dots, f_m) \subset S$ generated by generic homogeneous forms with $\deg f_i = d_i$ (i.e., the coefficients of the $f_i$ are general points in the corresponding affine space of coefficients). Set $R = S/I$, viewed as a graded $k$-algebra, and let $k$ denote the residue field $R/\mathfrak{m}$ where $\mathfrak{m}$ is the maximal homogeneous ideal of $R$. Define the graded Poincaré series of $k$ over $R$ by
$$P^R_k(t) \;=\; \sum_{i \ge 0} \dim_k \operatorname{Tor}^R_i(k,k)\, t^i,$$
and let $H_R(t) = \sum_{j \ge 0} \dim_k R_j\, t^j$ denote the Hilbert series of $R$.

Question: For $I$ generated by generic forms as above, is the Poincaré series $P^R_k(t)$ determined solely by the Hilbert series $H_R(t)$ (equivalently, by the numerical data $n$ and $d_1, \dots, d_m$)?

The question—whether the Poincaré series of $k$ over $R = S/I$ for $I$ generated by generic forms is determined by the Hilbert series of $R$—appears in published lists of open problems on syzygies and Hilbert functions and is closely tied to the still-open Fröberg conjecture on the Hilbert series of generic ideals (which itself is only known in special cases such as $m \le n+1$, equal degrees with $m$ large, and a few low-dimensional regimes). Consider the scalar distributed-delay Nicholson blowflies equation
  dN(t)/dt = -d N(t) + P ∫_{h(t)}^{t} N(u) e^{-N(u)} d_u R(t,u),  t ≥ t_0,
where d > 0 and P > 0 are constants, h: [t_0, ∞) → ℝ is a continuous nondecreasing delay function with h(t) ≤ t and lim_{t→∞} h(t) = ∞, and for each t the map u ↦ R(t,u) is nondecreasing on [h(t), t] with R(t,t) - R(t,h(t)) = 1, so that the integral is a probability-weighted average of N(u) e^{-N(u)} over the delay window [h(t), t]. Assume P > d so that the equation admits the positive equilibrium N* = ln(P/d).

A solution N(t) is called rapidly oscillating about N* if there exists T such that for all t ≥ T, any two consecutive zeros t_1 < t_2 of N(t) - N* satisfy t_2 - t_1 ≤ t_2 - h(t_2) (i.e. the distance between adjacent zeros is at most the prevailing delay).

Problem: Find sufficient conditions on the parameters d, P and on the delay distribution (h, R) such that the inequality
  P < d·e
implies the existence of at least one rapidly oscillating solution of the equation about N*.

representations.normalized:
Consider the linear Volterra functional integral equation with vanishing delay
$$u(t) = b(t)\,u(\theta(t)) + g(t) + (Vu)(t) + (V_\theta u)(t), \qquad t\in I:=[0,T],$$
where
$$(Vu)(t) = \int_0^t K_0(t,s)\,u(s)\,ds, \qquad (V_\theta u)(t) = \int_0^{\theta(t)} K_1(t,s)\,u(s)\,ds,$$
the delay function $\theta:I\to I$ is smooth, strictly increasing, satisfies $\theta(0)=0$, $0<\theta(t)<t$ for $t\in(0,T]$, and $0<\theta'(0)<1$ (so $\theta$ vanishes at $0$); the data $b,g\in C^\infty(I)$ and $K_0,K_1\in C^\infty(D)$ on the appropriate triangular/relevant domain $D$.

Fix an integer $N\ge 1$ and let $I_h$ be the uniform mesh $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N=T$, $t_n=nh$ with $h=T/N$, and set $\sigma_n:=(t_{n-1},t_n]$. Define the piecewise-polynomial space (discontinuous at mesh points)
$$S^{(-1)}_{m-1}(I_h) := \{v:I\to\mathbb{R} : v|_{\sigma_n}\in\mathcal{P}_{m-1},\ n=1,\dots,N\}.$$
Choose $m$ distinct collocation parameters $0<c_1<\cdots<c_m\le 1$ taken to be the $m$ Gauss points (the zeros of the shifted Legendre polynomial of degree $m$), and let
$$X_h := \{t_{n,i}=t_{n-1}+c_i h : n=1,\dots,N;\ i=1,\dots,m\}.$$
The collocation solution $u_h\in S^{(-1)}_{m-1}(I_h)$ is defined by enforcing
$$u_h(t) = b(t)\,u_h(\theta(t)) + g(t) + (Vu_h)(t) + (V_\theta u_h)(t) \quad\text{for all } t\in X_h.$$
The associated iterated collocation solution is
$$u_h^{\mathrm{it}}(t) := b(t)\,u_h(\theta(t)) + g(t) + (Vu_h)(t) + (V_\theta u_h)(t), \qquad t\in I.$$

It is known that when $b(t)\equiv 0$, on a uniform mesh and with $m$ Gauss collocation points, the iterated collocation solution attains the optimal local superconvergence estimate
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\bigl|u(t_n)-u_h^{\mathrm{it}}(t_n)\bigr| \le C\,h^{2m}.$$

Question: Does this optimal local error estimate continue to hold for the general equation above when $b(t)\not\equiv 0$ (with $b$ smooth)? That is, with the same uniform mesh and $m$ Gauss points, is there a constant $C>0$ independent of $h$ such that
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\bigl|u(t_n)-u_h^{\mathrm{it}}(t_n)\bigr| \le C\,h^{2m}\,?$$

  x'(t) = -δ(t) x(t) + Σ_{j=1}^m p_j(t) x(t-τ_j(t)) exp(-x(t-τ_j(t))),   t ≠ t_k,

with prescribed continuous, positive coefficients δ(t), p_j(t), continuous variable delays τ_j(t) ≥ 0, an unbounded increasing sequence of impulse times 0 < t_1 < t_2 < ... → ∞, and impulse multipliers a_k > 0. Allow also the distributed-delay version
  x'(t) = -δ(t) x(t) + ∫_0^∞ K(t,s) x(t-s) exp(-x(t-s)) ds,   t ≠ t_k,
with the same impulse rule x(t_k^+) = a_k x(t_k), where K is a nonnegative kernel.

(a) Establish existence of global positive solutions, permanence (uniform persistence and ultimate boundedness), stability of positive equilibria/solutions, and oscillation criteria for these impulsive variable-delay and distributed-delay Nicholson models.

(b) Assume that, in the absence of impulses (i.e. with all a_k = 1), the corresponding non-impulsive equation has a positive equilibrium that is globally asymptotically stable on the space of positive continuous initial functions. representations.normalized:
Consider the pantograph-type linear delay Volterra functional equations on the interval $I=[0,T]$:

(A) the delay differential equation
$$y'(t)=a(t)\,y(t)+b(t)\,y(qt)+f(t),\qquad t\in I,\quad y(0)=y_0,$$
and

(B) the second-kind Volterra integral equation with proportional vanishing delay
$$y(t)=g(t)+\int_{0}^{qt} K(t,s)\,y(s)\,ds,\qquad t\in I,$$

where $0<q<1$ is a fixed proportional-delay parameter and $a,b,f,g,K$ are given smooth functions.

Let $\Pi_N=\{0=t_0<t_1<\dots<t_N=T\}$ be the uniform mesh of $I$ with stepsize $h=T/N$, and let $S_m^{(d)}(\Pi_N)$ ($d\in\{-1,0\}$) denote the corresponding piecewise polynomial collocation space of degree $m\ge 1$. Choose collocation parameters $0<c_1<\dots<c_m\le 1$ equal to the Gauss(-Legendre) points and let $u_h\in S_m^{(d)}(\Pi_N)$ denote the collocation solution to the relevant equation.

Under standard regularity assumptions, it is known that for each fixed $q\in(0,1)$ there exists a constant $C_m(q)>0$, independent of $h$, such that the following optimal local superconvergence estimate holds at the mesh points:
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\bigl|\,y(t_n)-u_h(t_n)\,\bigr|\;\le\;C_m(q)\,h^{2m},\qquad h\to 0^{+}.$$

Let $C_m(q)$ denote, for each $m\ge 1$ and each $q\in(0,1)$, the smallest such constant for which this estimate is valid (in (A) and respectively in (B)).

Problem. Determine the explicit dependence of the best constants $C_m(q)$ on the proportional-delay parameter $q\in(0,1)$. In particular, analyse the asymptotic behaviour of $C_m(q)$ in the limit $q\to 1^{-}$: find sharp upper and lower bounds, or asymptotic equivalents, describing how $C_m(q)$ behaves as $q\to 1^{-}$ for each fixed $m\ge 1$.

Let $I=[0,T]$ and consider the linear Volterra functional integral equation
$$u(t) = b(t)\,u(\theta(t)) + g(t) + (Vu)(t) + (V_\theta u)(t), \qquad t\in I,$$
where $b,g\in C(I)$ with $|b(t)|<1$ on $I$, the delay function $\theta:I\to I$ is continuous with $\theta(0)=0$ and $0\le\theta(t)<t$ for $t>0$ (a vanishing delay; the prototypical case is $\theta(t)=qt$ with $0<q<1$), and the Volterra operators are
$$(Vu)(t)=\int_0^t K(t,s)u(s)\,ds, \qquad (V_\theta u)(t)=\int_0^{\theta(t)} K_\theta(t,s)u(s)\,ds,$$
with sufficiently smooth kernels $K,K_\theta$.

Introduce a uniform mesh $I_h:\,0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N=T$, $t_n=nh$, and the continuous piecewise polynomial space
$$S_m^{(0)}(I_h)=\{v\in C(I):\,v|_{[t_{n-1},t_n]}\in\Pi_m,\ n=1,\dots,N\}.$$
For prescribed collocation parameters $0<c_1<\cdots<c_m\le 1$, define the set of collocation points
$$X_h=\{t_{n-1}+c_i h:\ n=1,\dots,N,\ i=1,\dots,m\}.$$
The collocation solution $u_h\in S_m^{(0)}(I_h)$ is determined by the collocation equations
$$u_h(t)=b(t)u_h(\theta(t))+g(t)+(Vu_h)(t)+(V_\theta u_h)(t) \quad\text{for all }t\in X_h,$$
together with the initial condition $u_h(0)=g(0)/(1-b(0))$.

The iterated collocation solution is defined by
$$u_h^{it}(t):= b(t)u_h(\theta(t))+g(t)+(Vu_h)(t)+(V_\theta u_h)(t),\qquad t\in I.$$

Assume that for a suitable choice of the collocation parameters $\{c_i\}$ (e.g.\ Radau II or Gauss points), the collocation solution $u_h$ attains the known optimal local superconvergence orders at the mesh points (i.e.\ $\max_{0\le n\le N}|u(t_n)-u_h(t_n)|=O(h^{m+\kappa})$ for some $\kappa\ge 1$ characterizing the optimal local superconvergence).

Question: Does the iterated collocation solution $u_h^{it}$ retain these same optimal local superconvergence orders at the mesh points (and on $X_h$) as $u_h$, under the assumption $|b(t)|<1$ on $I$ and with the above initial value?

Let $k$ be a field and let $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ denote the polynomial ring in $n$ variables, graded by $\deg(x_i) = 1$ (or, more generally, by a positive $\mathbb{Z}^n$-grading). Recall that a monomial ideal $I \subset S$ is an ideal generated by monomials $x^{a} = x_1^{a_1} \cdots x_n^{a_n}$, and a toric ideal is the kernel $I_A = \ker(\pi_A)$ of a $k$-algebra homomorphism $\pi_A : k[y_1, \dots, y_m] \to k[t_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, t_d^{\pm 1}]$ sending $y_j \mapsto t^{a_j}$ for a finite set $A = \{a_1, \dots, a_m\} \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$. For a finitely generated graded $S$-module $M$, a minimal graded free resolution is an exact complex
$$ \cdots \to F_2 \to F_1 \to F_0 \to M \to 0, \qquad F_i = \bigoplus_{j} S(-j)^{\beta_{i,j}(M)}, $$
in which each differential has entries in the maximal homogeneous ideal; the numbers $\beta_{i,j}(M)$ are the graded Betti numbers of $M$.

Problem. Develop new explicit constructions and conceptual methods for producing minimal free resolutions of arbitrary monomial ideals $I \subset S$ and of arbitrary toric ideals $I_A$. In particular, find constructive recipes (for example combinatorial, topological, simplicial, cellular, discrete-Morse-theoretic, or algorithmic) that, given the generators of $I$ (respectively the matrix $A$), output the modules $F_i$ and the differentials of a minimal free resolution, and thereby determine the graded Betti numbers $\beta_{i,j}$ for all $i, j$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem of constructing minimal free resolutions of arbitrary monomial and toric ideals is a longstanding, broadly framed research direction. While many partial constructions exist (Taylor, Lyubeznik, Eliahou–Kirby, cellular and simplicial resolutions of Bayer–Sturmfels, lattice and CW resolutions of Batzies–Welker via discrete Morse theory, and recent advances such as the Eagon resolution and work on monomial ideals with linear quotients), no general construction is known. The question remains open as a guiding research program.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Many partial results are available: permanence, global asymptotic stability under various sufficient conditions, existence and exponential stability of (almost) periodic solutions, and Hopf bifurcation/chaos as the delay grows have been established in several works for Nicholson's blowflies models with nonlinear density-dependent mortality of the forms D(x)=ax/(x+b) and D(x)=a-b e^{-x}. However, a complete qualitative classification (sharp global stability thresholds, full bifurcation picture) remains open.

Consider the multi-delay pantograph-type Volterra functional integral equation
$$u(t)=g(t)+\sum_{j=1}^{r} b_j(t)\,u(\theta_j(t))+\sum_{j=1}^{r}(V_{\theta_j}u)(t),\qquad t\in I=[0,T],$$
where:
- $r\ge 2$ is an integer;
- the proportional (vanishing) delays are $\theta_j(t)=q_j t$ with $0<q_1<q_2<\cdots<q_r<1$;
- $g\in C^m(I)$ and $b_j\in C^m(I)$ are given smooth functions;
- each delay Volterra operator is
$$(V_{\theta_j}u)(t)=\int_{0}^{\theta_j(t)} K_j(t,s)\,u(s)\,ds,$$
with smooth kernels $K_j$.

Fix a uniform mesh $I_N=\{t_n=nh:\ n=0,1,\dots,N,\ h=T/N\}$ and a set of collocation parameters $0\le c_1<c_2<\cdots<c_m\le 1$. Let $S_{m-1}^{(-1)}(I_N)$ denote the space of (possibly discontinuous) piecewise polynomials of degree at most $m-1$ on $I_N$. Let $u_h\in S_{m-1}^{(-1)}(I_N)$ be the collocation solution defined by requiring the equation to hold at the collocation points $t_{n,i}=t_n+c_i h$, and let $u_h^{\mathrm{it}}$ denote the corresponding iterated collocation solution obtained by substituting $u_h$ into the right-hand side.

Determine the optimal global order of convergence
$$\|u-u_h\|_{\infty}=O(h^{p})\quad\text{and}\quad \|u-u_h^{\mathrm{it}}\|_{\infty}=O(h^{p'})$$
and the optimal local (mesh-point) orders
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}|u(t_n)-u_h(t_n)|=O(h^{q}),\qquad \max_{0\le n\le N}|u(t_n)-u_h^{\mathrm{it}}(t_n)|=O(h^{q'})$$
attainable on uniform meshes, in terms of $m$, the collocation parameters $\{c_i\}$, and the delay ratios $\{q_j\}$.

Let $0<q<1$ and let $\theta(t)=qt$. Consider the neutral Volterra functional integro-differential equation
$$u'(t)=a(t)u(t)+b(t)u(\theta(t))+c(t)u'(\theta(t))+\int_0^t\!\big[K_{0,0}(t,s)u(s)+K_{0,1}(t,s)u'(s)\big]ds+\int_0^{\theta(t)}\!\big[K_{1,0}(t,s)u(s)+K_{1,1}(t,s)u'(s)\big]ds,\qquad t\in I:=[0,T],$$
together with the initial condition $u(0)=u_0$, where the coefficients $a,b,c$ and the kernels $K_{i,j}$ ($i,j\in\{0,1\}$) are sufficiently smooth on $I$ and on $\{(t,s):0\le s\le t\le T\}$ respectively.

Let $I_h=\{t_n=nh:0\le n\le N,\;Nh=T\}$ be a uniform mesh on $I$ and set $\sigma_n=(t_n,t_{n+1}]$. For an integer $m\ge1$ and collocation parameters $0<c_1<\cdots<c_m\le 1$, the collocation space is
$$S_m^{(0)}(I_h)=\{v\in C(I):v|_{\sigma_n}\in\pi_m,\ 0\le n\le N-1\},$$
where $\pi_m$ denotes polynomials of degree at most $m$. Let $u_h\in S_m^{(0)}(I_h)$ be the collocation solution determined by requiring that $u_h$ satisfies the equation above (with $u$ replaced by $u_h$) at the collocation points $t_{n,i}:=t_n+c_i h$, and that $u_h(0)=u_0$. Choose the $\{c_i\}$ as the $m$ Gauss points (zeros of the shifted Legendre polynomial of degree $m$ on $[0,1]$).

Define the optimal order of pointwise superconvergence on $I_h$ as the largest $p^*$ such that
$$\max_{t\in I_h}|u(t)-u_h(t)|\le C_m(q)\,h^{p^*}$$
holds for all sufficiently smooth data, with $C_m(q)$ independent of $h$.

(a) Prove or disprove that
$$p^*=\begin{cases}2m,&m=1,2,\\ m+2,&m>2.\end{cases}$$
(b) Determine whether there exist choices of collocation parameters $\{c_i\}$ such that the same estimate is valid with $u(t)-u_h(t)$ replaced by $u'(t)-u'_h(t)$ at the points of $I_h$.

Let $G = (V, E)$ be a finite simple graph with vertex set $V = \{x_1, \dots, x_n\}$, and let $k$ be a field. The edge ideal of $G$ is the squarefree monomial ideal
$$I(G) = (x_i x_j : \{x_i, x_j\} \in E) \subseteq S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n].$$
The Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of $I(G)$ is defined as
$$\operatorname{reg}(I(G)) = \max\{ j - i : \beta_{i,j}(S/I(G)) \neq 0 \},$$
where $\beta_{i,j}$ are the graded Betti numbers of $S/I(G)$ over $S$.

Problem: Determine a closed-form formula, or at least a sharp upper bound, for $\operatorname{reg}(I(G))$ expressed purely in terms of combinatorial invariants of $G$ (such as the matching number, induced matching number, independence number, chromatic invariants, or forbidden induced subgraph data), that is valid for every finite simple graph $G$.

Determining the regularity of edge ideals from combinatorial data of the underlying graph remains an active and largely open research area. While many partial results are known (e.g., Fröberg's theorem characterizing linear resolutions, Hà–Van Tuyl's lower bound by the induced matching number, sharp bounds for specific classes such as chordal graphs, bipartite graphs, and lobsters, and recent work on powers of edge ideals), no general formula or sharp universal upper bound in terms of graph invariants is currently known for arbitrary graphs.

Consider the linear weakly singular Volterra functional integro-differential equation
  u'(t) = a(t) u(t) + b(t) u(θ(t)) + g(t) + (V_α u)(t) + (V_{θ,α} u)(t),    t ∈ I := [0, T],
with initial condition u(0) = u_0, where
  (V_α u)(t)     = ∫_0^{t}    (t − s)^{−α} K_0(t, s) u(s) ds,
  (V_{θ,α} u)(t) = ∫_0^{θ(t)} (t − s)^{−α} K_1(t, s) u(s) ds,
and 0 < α < 1. Assume the coefficient functions a, b, g and the kernels K_0, K_1 have continuous derivatives of order m + 1 on their respective domains. The vanishing delay θ ∈ C^{m+1}(I) satisfies
  (N1) θ(0) = 0 and 0 < θ(t) < t for all t ∈ (0, T];
  (N2) θ is strictly increasing on I with θ'(t) > 0.

Let N ≥ 1 and consider the graded mesh
  I_h = { t_n := (n/N)^r T : 0 ≤ n ≤ N },
with grading exponent r ≥ 1. Let σ_n := (t_n, t_{n+1}], and fix collocation parameters 0 ≤ c_1 < c_2 < ⋯ < c_m ≤ 1, generating the collocation points t_{n,i} := t_n + c_i (t_{n+1} − t_n). Define the piecewise polynomial space
  S_m^{(0)}(I_h) := { v ∈ C(I) : v|_{σ_n} ∈ π_m for 0 ≤ n ≤ N − 1 },
where π_m denotes polynomials of degree ≤ m. Let u_h ∈ S_m^{(0)}(I_h) be the collocation solution determined by u_h(0) = u_0 and
  u_h'(t_{n,i}) = a(t_{n,i}) u_h(t_{n,i}) + b(t_{n,i}) u_h(θ(t_{n,i})) + g(t_{n,i}) + (V_α u_h)(t_{n,i}) + (V_{θ,α} u_h)(t_{n,i}).

Question. Assume the collocation parameters {c_i} satisfy
  ∫_0^1 ∏_{i=1}^{m} (s − c_i) ds = 0,
and that the grading exponent satisfies r ≥ (m + 1 − α)/(2 − α). Does the global error estimate
  ‖u − u_h‖_∞ ≤ C_m(r) N^{−(m+1−α)}
hold for every α ∈ (0, 1), with a constant C_m(r) independent of N?

The question is posed as a conjecture on the attainable global convergence order of piecewise polynomial collocation, on graded meshes with optimally chosen exponent, for weakly singular Volterra functional integro-differential equations with a vanishing delay. Related results have been obtained for delay Volterra integral equations with weakly singular kernels and for VIDEs without delay on graded meshes, and a 1997 Brunner conjecture on local superconvergence for proportional-delay VIEs has been resolved. However, no source located explicitly confirms or refutes this particular conjecture for the full weakly singular VFIDE in the stated S_m^{(0)} collocation setting with the precise grading bound r ≥ (m+1−α)/(2−α). The status is therefore taken to be unknown / likely still open.

Recall that a (finite) cellular resolution, in the sense of Bayer–Sturmfels, is a free resolution of a monomial quotient $S/J'$ over $S$ whose differentials are encoded by the cellular chain complex of a labeled CW-complex, with the resolution being supported on that complex.

Develop a theory of infinite cellular resolutions that supports minimal free resolutions of monomial ideals over quotient rings $R = S/I$, in particular:

(a) Define an appropriate notion of an (infinite) labeled CW-complex (or more general cell-like combinatorial object) whose associated chain complex, suitably homogenized over $R$, yields a free resolution of $R/J$ as an $R$-module.

(b) Show that, for every monomial ideal $J$ in such a quotient ring $R$ (with $I$ monomial, and separately with $I$ toric), the minimal free $R$-resolution of $R/J$ can be realized as such an infinite cellular resolution.

(c) Identify combinatorial/topological invariants of the supporting cell complex that compute the multigraded Betti numbers of $R/J$ over $R$.

A function $C:[0,1]^n\to[0,1]$ (with $n\ge 2$) is called an $n$-ary copula if it is grounded (equal to $0$ whenever some argument is $0$), has $1$ as a neutral element in each coordinate (i.e. $C(1,\dots,1,x,1,\dots,1)=x$), and is $n$-increasing in the sense that for every $n$-box $\prod_{i=1}^n[a_i,b_i]\subseteq[0,1]^n$ the associated $C$-volume is nonnegative. Such a $C$ is said to be associative in the sense of Post if for every integer $n\ge 3$ and all $x_1,\dots,x_{2n-1}\in[0,1]$,
$$C\bigl(C(x_1,\dots,x_n),x_{n+1},\dots,x_{2n-1}\bigr)=C\bigl(x_1,C(x_2,\dots,x_{n+1}),x_{n+2},\dots,x_{2n-1}\bigr)=\cdots=C\bigl(x_1,\dots,x_{n-1},C(x_n,\dots,x_{2n-1})\bigr),$$
i.e. all ways of applying $C$ to a single consecutive block of $n$ of the $2n-1$ inputs and then applying $C$ to the resulting $n$ values yield the same number.

For a fixed integer $n\ge 3$, give a structural characterization (representation theorem) of all $n$-ary copulas $C:[0,1]^n\to[0,1]$ that are associative in the sense of Post, analogous to the Ling-type Archimedean/ordinal-sum classification of binary associative copulas.

Let $I=[0,T]$ with $T>0$, and let $\theta:I\to I$ be a vanishing delay function satisfying:
(i) $\theta(0)=0$;
(ii) there exists $q_1\in(0,1)$ such that $\theta(t)\le q_1 t$ for all $t\in I$;
(iii) $\theta\in C^d(I)$ for some integer $d\ge 1$;
but $\theta$ is NOT assumed to be strictly increasing on $I$ (so $\theta$ may have intervals of constancy or local decrease).

Consider the Volterra functional integro-differential equation (VFIDE)
$$y'(t)=a(t)y(t)+b(t)y(\theta(t))+\int_{\theta(t)}^{t} K(t,s,y(s))\,ds,\qquad t\in I,\quad y(0)=y_0,$$
and the Volterra functional integral equation (VFIE)
$$y(t)=g(t)+\int_{\theta(t)}^{t} K(t,s,y(s))\,ds,\qquad t\in I,$$
with sufficiently smooth data $a,b,g,K$.

Given a mesh $0=t_0<t_1<\dots<t_N=T$ and an integer $m\ge 1$, let $S_m^{(0)}$ (resp. $S_m^{(-1)}$) denote the space of continuous (resp. discontinuous) piecewise polynomials of degree $\le m$ on the mesh, and consider the collocation solution determined by $m$ collocation parameters $0<c_1<\dots<c_m\le 1$.

Establish a convergence theory (global convergence orders, and where possible local superconvergence at mesh points) for the piecewise-polynomial collocation solutions of the above VFIDE and VFIE under conditions (i)–(iii) but WITHOUT the assumption that $\theta$ is strictly increasing on $I$. In particular, identify appropriate mesh constructions (e.g., quasi-$\theta$-invariant meshes) under which optimal-order convergence and superconvergence results, analogous to those known in the strictly increasing case, continue to hold.

Let $k$ be a field and let $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring. A monomial ideal $L \subset S$ is called a lex ideal if for every monomial $m \in L$ and every monomial $m'$ of the same degree as $m$ with $m' >_{\mathrm{lex}} m$, one has $m' \in L$ (here $>_{\mathrm{lex}}$ denotes the lexicographic order with $x_1 > x_2 > \cdots > x_n$).

Consider a standard graded $k$-algebra quotient $R = S/J$ where $J$ is one of the following:
(i) the defining ideal of a Veronese ring, i.e., $R$ is the $d$-th Veronese subring $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]^{(d)}$ presented as a quotient of a polynomial ring by its toric relations, for some integers $n \geq 2$ and $d \geq 2$; or
(ii) the defining ideal of a Segre ring, i.e., $R$ is the Segre product $k[x_1,\dots,x_a] \# k[y_1,\dots,y_b]$ presented as a quotient of a polynomial ring by the $2 \times 2$ minors of a generic $a \times b$ matrix.

Let $\overline{L}$ denote the image in $R$ of a lex ideal $L$ (with respect to a chosen monomial structure on $R$). Explicitly describe, in closed combinatorial form, the minimal graded free resolution $G_\bullet$ of $R/\overline{L}$ as an $R$-module: in particular, give formulas for the graded Betti numbers $\beta^R_{i,j}(R/\overline{L})$ and the differentials of $G_\bullet$, for every lex ideal $\overline{L}$ in the quotient ring $R$.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ denote the set of bivariate copulas, i.e., functions $C:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ such that $C(x,0)=C(0,y)=0$, $C(x,1)=x$, $C(1,y)=y$, and $C$ is 2-increasing: $C(x_2,y_2)-C(x_2,y_1)-C(x_1,y_2)+C(x_1,y_1)\ge 0$ for all $x_1\le x_2$, $y_1\le y_2$ in $[0,1]$.

A copula $C$ is called associative if $C(C(x,y),z)=C(x,C(y,z))$ for all $x,y,z\in[0,1]$; equivalently, $C$ is a 1-Lipschitz triangular norm. Let $\mathcal{C}_a$ denote the class of associative bivariate copulas.

A copula $C$ is called commutative if $C(x,y)=C(y,x)$ for all $x,y\in[0,1]$. It is called Schur-concave if $C(x,y)\le C(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y,\lambda y+(1-\lambda)x)$ for all $x,y\in[0,1]$ and all $\lambda\in[0,1]$.

Let $\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}_a$ be the closure, under uniform convergence on $[0,1]^2$, of the set of all finite convex combinations of elements of $\mathcal{C}_a$. Determine whether $\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}_a$ coincides exactly with the class of all bivariate copulas that are both Schur-concave and commutative.

Consider the linear scalar Volterra functional integro-differential test equation with a vanishing proportional delay
  u'(t) = a u(t) + b u(qt) + \int_0^t k_0(t-s) u(s)\,ds + \int_0^{qt} k_1(t-s) u(s)\,ds,  t \ge 0,
where a, b \in \mathbb{R}, q \in (0,1) is a fixed proportionality constant, u(0) = u_0 \in \mathbb{R}, and k_0, k_1 are real-valued convolution kernels defined on [0, \infty), assumed to be either continuous or weakly singular (i.e. of the form k_i(\tau) = \tau^{-\alpha_i} K_i(\tau) with 0 < \alpha_i < 1 and K_i continuous and bounded). Assume that the coefficients a and b are such that the underlying pantograph equation v'(t) = a v(t) + b v(qt), t \ge 0, is asymptotically stable, i.e. every solution v satisfies \lim_{t\to\infty} v(t) = 0.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the kernel pair (k_0, k_1) (within the continuous and the weakly singular classes) under which every nontrivial solution u of the integro-differential equation above still satisfies
  \lim_{t\to\infty} u(t) = 0.

A bivariate copula is a function $C:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ satisfying (i) $C(x,0)=C(0,x)=0$ and $C(x,1)=C(1,x)=x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$, and (ii) the 2-increasing property $C(x_2,y_2)-C(x_2,y_1)-C(x_1,y_2)+C(x_1,y_1)\ge 0$ whenever $0\le x_1\le x_2\le 1$ and $0\le y_1\le y_2\le 1$. A continuous semicopula is a continuous function $S:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ that is non-decreasing in each argument and satisfies $S(x,1)=S(1,x)=x$ and $S(x,0)=S(0,x)=0$.

Given a strictly increasing bijection $\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ (necessarily continuous) and a copula $C$, define the transformed binary operation
$$C_\varphi(x,y)\;:=\;\varphi^{-1}\bigl(C(\varphi(x),\varphi(y))\bigr),\qquad (x,y)\in[0,1]^2.$$
Let
$$\mathcal C^* \;=\; \{\,C_\varphi : C\text{ is a bivariate copula and }\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]\text{ is a strictly increasing bijection}\,\}.$$
It is known that $C_\varphi$ need not itself be a copula and that $\mathcal C^*$ is strictly contained in the class of continuous semicopulas.

Problem: Give an intrinsic characterization of the class $\mathcal C^*$, i.e., describe necessary and sufficient conditions on a continuous semicopula $S:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ so that $S=C_\varphi$ for some bivariate copula $C$ and some strictly increasing bijection $\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$.

Consider the linear Volterra functional equation with vanishing delay
   y(t) = a(t) y(t) + b(t) y(θ(t)) + (V y)(t) + (V_θ y)(t) + f(t),  t ∈ [0,∞),
or, in the differential case,
   y'(t) = a(t) y(t) + b(t) y(θ(t)) + (V y)(t) + (V_θ y)(t) + f(t),  y(0) = y_0,
where (V y)(t) = ∫_0^t K(t,s) y(s) ds and (V_θ y)(t) = ∫_0^{θ(t)} K_θ(t,s) y(s) ds, with sufficiently smooth coefficients and kernels, and θ:[0,∞)→[0,∞) is a vanishing delay function.

Assume that θ satisfies the following conditions:
 (N1) θ ∈ C([0,∞)) ∩ C^1((0,∞)), θ(0) = 0, and 0 < θ(t) < t for all t > 0;
 (N2) θ'(t) > 0 for all t > 0, and θ'(t) is bounded on every compact subinterval of (0,∞);
 (N3) lim_{t→0+} θ(t)/t = q for some constant q ∈ (0,1), so that θ behaves asymptotically like a proportional (pantograph-type) delay near 0.

For the special proportional case θ(t) = q t with 0 < q < 1, suppose that complete answers are known to the following two asymptotic-stability questions:
 (P1) Characterize the values of the mesh parameters and the coefficients (a, b, kernels) for which the exact solution y(t) → 0 as t → ∞.
 (P2) Characterize the values of the mesh parameters and method parameters (e.g., collocation parameters on a quasi-geometric or uniform mesh) for which the piecewise polynomial collocation approximation u_h(t) → 0 as t → ∞, and determine whether this asymptotic stability is preserved by the fully discretized scheme.

Question: Do the answers obtained for θ(t) = q t in (P1) and (P2) remain valid, without modification, when θ is replaced by an arbitrary nonlinear delay function satisfying (N1)–(N3)? If not, determine the precise modifications required.

Let $n\ge 2$. An $n$-ary semicopula is a function $S:[0,1]^n\to[0,1]$ such that:
(i) $S(x_1,\dots,x_n)=0$ whenever $x_i=0$ for some $i$;
(ii) $S(1,\dots,1,x_i,1,\dots,1)=x_i$ for every $i$ and every $x_i\in[0,1]$ (each variable is neutral at $1$);
(iii) $S$ is nondecreasing in each variable.

For an $n$-dimensional Cartesian interval $R=\prod_{i=1}^n[a_i,b_i]\subseteq[0,1]^n$ with $a_i\le b_i$, the $S$-volume of $R$ is
$$V_S(R)=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^n}(-1)^{n-\sum_i\varepsilon_i}\, S\bigl(c_1(\varepsilon_1),\dots,c_n(\varepsilon_n)\bigr),$$
where $c_i(0)=a_i$ and $c_i(1)=b_i$.

Let $\mathcal G$ denote the class of all $n$-ary semicopulas $S$ such that $V_S(R)\ge 0$ for every $n$-dimensional Cartesian interval $R=\prod_{i=1}^n[a_i,1]\subseteq[0,1]^n$ whose top vertex equals the top vertex $(1,1,\dots,1)$ of the unit hypercube.

Problem: Provide an intrinsic characterization of the class $\mathcal G$, and characterize natural distinguished subclasses of $\mathcal G$ (for example, those obtained by imposing additional symmetry, continuity, associativity, or Lipschitz-type conditions).

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a central hyperplane arrangement in a complex vector space, and let $A = \mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{A})$ denote its Orlik–Solomon algebra (the quotient of the exterior algebra on generators $e_H$, one per hyperplane $H \in \mathcal{A}$, by the ideal generated by $\partial(e_{H_1}\cdots e_{H_k})$ for every dependent subarrangement $\{H_1,\dots,H_k\}$). Let $\mathrm{Hilb}_A(t) = \sum_i \dim(A_i) t^i$ be its Hilbert series. The complement $M(\mathcal{A})$ has fundamental group whose lower central series quotients have ranks $\phi_j$. The arrangement is said to satisfy the lower central series (LCS) formula if
$$\prod_{j \ge 1} (1 - t^j)^{\phi_j} \;=\; \mathrm{Hilb}_A(-t).$$
An arrangement is supersolvable if its intersection lattice admits a maximal chain of modular elements.

Exhibit a central hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ that is not supersolvable but for which the LCS formula above holds; equivalently, exhibit a central arrangement whose Orlik–Solomon algebra is Koszul yet admits no presentation with a quadratic Gröbner basis (or prove that no such arrangement exists, thereby establishing that Koszulness of $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{A})$ implies supersolvability of $\mathcal{A}$).

Consider the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation on the real line,
   u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = 0,   x ∈ ℝ, t ∈ ℝ,
with initial condition u(x,0) = u_0(x). Recall that a bounded continuous function f : ℝ → ℝ is almost periodic (in the sense of Bohr) if for every ε > 0 the set of ε-almost-periods {τ ∈ ℝ : sup_{x∈ℝ} |f(x+τ) − f(x)| < ε} is relatively dense in ℝ; equivalently, the set of translates {f(· + s) : s ∈ ℝ} is precompact in the uniform topology on ℝ.

Suppose u_0 is almost periodic. Decide whether the following statement is true: for every almost periodic initial datum u_0, there exists a global solution u(x,t) of the KdV equation with u(·,0) = u_0 such that for every t ∈ ℝ the function x ↦ u(x,t) is almost periodic, and moreover for every fixed x ∈ ℝ the function t ↦ u(x,t) is almost periodic.

Let V be a finite set of biological entities (e.g., genes or proteins). Suppose we are given:

(1) A biological network graph G1 = (V, E1) representing known structural relationships such as a pathway, possibly equipped with a pre-existing layout L1 : V → R^2 that assigns each node a position in the plane.

(2) A weighted correlation graph G2 = (V, E2, w) on the same node set V, where each edge {u,v} ∈ E2 carries a weight w(u,v) ∈ R representing a statistically significant correlation between u and v (for instance, significant co-up-regulation or co-down-regulation of expression, or sufficient agreement of annotations across attributes such as genotype, time point, or biological replicate). Edges that fail a chosen significance threshold are excluded from E2.

The problem is to design an algorithm that produces either:
(a) a single planar drawing of the union graph G = (V, E1 ∪ E2), in which the two edge sets E1 and E2 are rendered so as to be visually distinguishable; or
(b) two drawings of G1 and G2 respectively that share an identical node-coordinate map φ : V → R^2,

subject to the following objectives:

(i) Both the structure of G1 and the correlation structure of G2 should be clearly readable in the resulting drawing(s).
(ii) The drawing should deviate from the given pre-existing layout L1 of G1 as little as possible, under a suitable quantitative measure (e.g., sum of squared displacements ∑_{v∈V} ‖φ(v) − L1(v)‖^2).
(iii) The correlation edges E2 (especially those with high |w|) should be emphasized, for example by minimizing a stress-like functional that penalizes large geometric distance between strongly correlated node pairs.

Formulate and solve: produce an algorithm (and an associated objective function balancing (ii) and (iii)) that, given (G1, L1, G2, w), outputs a coordinate map φ : V → R^2 (and a rendering style for the two edge sets in case (a)) meeting the above criteria, together with guarantees on readability and on preservation of L1.

Let $W_N = (w_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le N}$ be a sequence of $N\times N$ real symmetric (or complex Hermitian) random matrices whose entries on and above the diagonal are independent (up to the symmetry constraint), have mean zero, and have variances $\sigma_{ij}^2 = \mathbb{E}|w_{ij}|^2$ chosen so that the empirical spectral measure of $W_N/\sqrt{N}$ converges weakly almost surely to a deterministic compactly supported probability measure $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}$ (the equilibrium / self-consistent density of states), and such that higher moments of the entries satisfy standard sub-exponential tail bounds. Assume that the support of $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is a finite disjoint union of more than one interval, i.e.\
$$\mathrm{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}) = \bigcup_{k=1}^{p}[a_k,b_k], \qquad p\ge 2, \qquad b_k<a_{k+1}.$$

Prove the following local spectral universality statements for the eigenvalues $\lambda_1\le\dots\le\lambda_N$ of $W_N/\sqrt{N}$:

(a) (Bulk universality.) For every $E$ in the interior of $\mathrm{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}})$ and every fixed $k\ge 1$, the rescaled $k$-point correlation function of the eigenvalues near $E$ converges, as $N\to\infty$, to the corresponding sine-kernel determinantal/Pfaffian correlation function of the GUE (in the complex Hermitian case) or GOE (in the real symmetric case).

(b) (Edge universality at every edge.) For each $k\in\{1,\dots,p\}$ and at both endpoints $a_k$ and $b_k$ of every connected component of $\mathrm{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}})$ — including the internal edges $b_1,a_2,b_2,\dots,a_p$ as well as the two external edges $a_1$ and $b_p$ — the appropriately rescaled extremal eigenvalues of $W_N/\sqrt{N}$ near that edge converge in distribution to the Tracy–Widom law of the corresponding symmetry class (TW$_2$ in the complex Hermitian case, TW$_1$ in the real symmetric case).

Let G = (V, E) be a large graph (intended to model a biological network) in which every vertex v ∈ V and every edge e ∈ E is decorated with a tuple of attributes drawn from heterogeneous data types, including: (i) nominal attributes (e.g. labels or categories), (ii) ordinal attributes (e.g. rankings or partial orders coming from ontologies), (iii) scalar attributes (real-valued measurements, ratios, or comparisons), (iv) categorized spatial attributes (locations or regions belonging to a finite set of categories), (v) time-series attributes (functions t ↦ x_v(t) or t ↦ x_e(t) sampled at finitely many time points), and (vi) uncertain attributes (values equipped with probability distributions or error intervals).

Design a visual encoding scheme Φ that maps G together with all of its attributes to a planar layout with associated graphical marks, satisfying the following requirements:

1. Φ chooses, for each attribute type listed above, a visual channel (e.g. hue, luminance, shape, size, orientation, texture, position) or composite glyph, and specifies whether the channel is attached to the node mark, to the edge mark, or to a coordinated auxiliary view.

2. Φ enables a viewer to identify, at the scale of the entire graph, sets of co-regulated elements — i.e. groups of nodes or edges whose time-series and scalar attributes are correlated above a chosen threshold — together with the topological connections among them.

3. Φ uses preattentive visual features (features detectable in less than ~250 ms without serial search) for the comparisons that must be performed across the whole graph.

4. Φ avoids the failure mode in which small per-node embedded graphics (e.g. miniature time-series plots) become too small to be visually compared in a large graph, and simultaneously avoids the opposite failure mode in which information is split across so many coordinated views that the cross-view linking cost dominates.

Provide such a scheme Φ together with a precise specification of which visual channels are assigned to which attribute types, when integrated node/edge encodings are used versus coordinated multiple views, and a justification (theoretical or empirical) that the resulting representation simultaneously meets requirements (1)–(4).

Let G = (V, E) be a very large graph (with up to thousands of vertices and edges) representing a biological network, equipped with a hierarchical decomposition H whose nodes correspond to semantically meaningful substructures (pathways and subpathways). Let G_1, …, G_k be designated subgraphs of G (e.g., pathways), which need not be pairwise disjoint: a vertex v may belong to several G_i, in which case the multiple occurrences represent the same biological entity. Some of the G_i may come with a prescribed internal layout or with prescribed relative positions to other G_j.

Develop a visualization and navigation framework, i.e., an algorithm that produces a sequence of drawings of G (and of subsystems of the G_i) together with interactive operations, satisfying all of the following requirements:

1. Overview/backbone abstraction: produce a readable abstracted drawing summarizing the G_i and the interrelations (edges of G between different G_i, and shared vertices among overlapping G_i).
2. Navigation: support interactive transitions from a currently displayed set of subsets G_{i_1}, …, G_{i_r} to a related set (e.g., neighboring or connected pathways), with smooth visual continuity.
3. Stability: after each user interaction the drawing should change only locally and minimally (mental-map preservation), and prescribed drawing conventions for biological networks and prescribed internal layouts of the G_i must be respected.
4. Expand-and-collapse: support expand and collapse operations, but only along the hierarchical decomposition H (i.e., only semantically meaningful substructures may be collapsed), and integrate these operations into the layout algorithm while preserving the conventions and mental map.
5. Context: while focusing on certain G_i, provide appropriate contextual information about the surrounding network.
6. Duplicates: provide a principled visual treatment of vertices that occur in several overlapping G_i, making clear when distinct on-screen occurrences represent the same biological entity.

Provide such a framework, prove guarantees on the layouts it produces (readability, stability under interaction, and complexity), and demonstrate its applicability to biological networks of the stated scale.

Let $\beta>0$. For each $N\ge 1$, let $\lambda_{\max}^{(N,\beta)}$ denote the largest eigenvalue of the Gaussian $\beta$-ensemble of size $N$ — that is, the joint density on $\mathbb{R}^N$ proportional to
$$\prod_{1\le i<j\le N}|\lambda_i-\lambda_j|^{\beta}\,\exp\Big(-\tfrac{\beta N}{4}\sum_{i=1}^N \lambda_i^2\Big).$$
It is known that the rescaled top eigenvalue $N^{2/3}(\lambda_{\max}^{(N,\beta)}-2)$ converges in distribution to a limiting law $F_\beta$, the general-$\beta$ Tracy–Widom distribution (which for $\beta=1,2,4$ recovers the classical Tracy–Widom laws).

Heuristic loop-equation/topological-expansion arguments propose a detailed all-orders asymptotic expansion for the right tail of $F_\beta$ of the form
$$1-F_\beta(t) \;\sim\; \frac{C_\beta}{t^{3\beta/4}}\,\exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{2}{3}\beta\, t^{3/2}\Big)\,\Big(1+\sum_{k\ge 1}\frac{a_k(\beta)}{t^{3k/2}}\Big)\qquad (t\to +\infty),$$
together with a corresponding all-orders expansion of the left tail as $t\to -\infty$, with explicit coefficients $C_\beta$ and $a_k(\beta)$ produced by the loop-equation recursion.

Problem. Establish these proposed asymptotic expansions for the tails of $F_\beta$ rigorously, for every $\beta>0$.

The leading-order right tail exponent of the general-$\beta$ Tracy–Widom law was proved rigorously by Dumaz and Virág (2013) via the stochastic Airy operator. Rigorous all-orders expansions are known for the classical cases $\beta=1,2,4$ (and $\beta=6$ via Calogero–Painlevé/Riemann–Hilbert methods of Bertola–Cafasso–Rubtsov and Grava–Its–Kapaev–Mezzadri). However, the full detailed all-orders asymptotic expansions conjectured by Borot–Eynard–Majumdar–Nadal for general $\beta>0$ have not been rigorously established in full generality; the problem remains open in this stronger form.

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be an open set, and let $B \in BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d) \cap L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d)$ be a vector field of locally bounded variation. Suppose there exists a measurable function $\rho \in L^\infty(\Omega)$ and a constant $C>0$ with $\rho \geq C$ almost everywhere, such that the product $\rho B$ is divergence-free in the sense of distributions:
$$D \cdot (\rho B) = 0 \quad \text{in } \mathcal{D}'(\Omega).$$
The distributional divergence $D \cdot B$ is a Radon measure on $\Omega$, and admits a Lebesgue decomposition into an absolutely continuous part, a jump part, and a Cantor part $D^c \cdot B$. Let $\widetilde{B}$ denote the precise representative of $B$, and define the tangential set of $B$ as
$$E := \{ x \in \Omega : \text{ for } |D B|\text{-a.e.\ matrix valued density } M(x), \ M(x)\cdot \widetilde{B}(x) = 0 \},$$
i.e.\ the set on which the polar of $DB$ annihilates $\widetilde B$.

Question: Does the total variation measure $|D^c \cdot B|$ vanish on the tangential set $E$ of $B$?

The question is a well-known open problem in the theory of nearly incompressible BV vector fields, formulated by De Lellis and collaborators in connection with Bressan's compactness conjecture and the DiPerna–Lions theory. Subsequent work (Bianchini–Gusev, Bianchini–Bonicatto) established renormalization and uniqueness results for steady and autonomous nearly incompressible BV fields in two dimensions, and counterexamples exist for general BV fields without the nearly-incompressible assumption. However, no search result indicates a positive resolution in the general nearly incompressible setting, and the problem appears to remain open.

Consider directed last-passage percolation on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2$ defined as follows. Let $\{w(i,j) : (i,j) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2\}$ be a family of i.i.d. nonnegative random variables with common distribution $F$ (the "weights"). For $(m,n) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2$, define the last-passage time
$$ L(m,n) \;=\; \max_{\pi:(0,0)\to(m,n)} \sum_{(i,j)\in\pi} w(i,j), $$
where the maximum is taken over all up-right lattice paths $\pi$ from $(0,0)$ to $(m,n)$ (i.e. paths that at each step increase exactly one coordinate by $1$).

The Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) universality conjecture predicts the following "3:2:1" scaling behaviour for $L$. There exist a deterministic constant $\mu = \mu(F) > 0$ (the time constant in the direction $(1,1)$) and constants $c_1, c_2 > 0$ such that:

(i) Fluctuation exponent $1/3$: as $N \to \infty$,
$$ \frac{L(N,N) - \mu N}{c_1 N^{1/3}} \;\Longrightarrow\; \mathrm{TW}_{\mathrm{GUE}}, $$
where $\mathrm{TW}_{\mathrm{GUE}}$ denotes the Tracy–Widom GUE distribution.

(ii) Transversal/correlation exponent $2/3$: the typical transversal fluctuations of the maximising path from $(0,0)$ to $(N,N)$ are of order $N^{2/3}$, and on the spatial scale $N^{2/3}$ the rescaled fluctuation field converges (in an appropriate sense) to the Airy$_2$ process; equivalently, with $t$ playing the role of the longitudinal coordinate, the scaled process
$$ \frac{L(N + \lfloor c_2 x N^{2/3}\rfloor,\, N - \lfloor c_2 x N^{2/3}\rfloor) - \mu_x N}{c_1 N^{1/3}} $$
converges as $N\to\infty$ to the Airy$_2$ process in $x$ (minus a parabola), reflecting the 3:2:1 scaling of fluctuation:transversal:longitudinal coordinates.

Question. Does (i)–(ii) hold for last-passage percolation with general weight distributions $F$? More precisely, identify a natural class of weight distributions $F$ (for example, all continuous distributions with sufficiently many moments and no atom at the top of the support) for which one can prove that $L$ exhibits the full 3:2:1 KPZ scaling described above, with the Tracy–Widom GUE one-point limit and the Airy$_2$ correlation structure.

KPZ universality with full 3:2:1 scaling for last-passage percolation is rigorously established only for special integrable weight distributions (notably exponential and geometric). For general weights the conjecture remains widely cited as a central open problem; recent work (e.g. convex upper bounds, hierarchical environments, partial universality results for tilted/perturbed integrable models) makes partial progress but does not resolve the conjecture.

Let $\mathcal{L} = (L_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ be an indexed family of recursive languages, where each $L_i \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is uniformly decidable in $i$. A text for a language $L$ is an infinite sequence $t = t_0, t_1, t_2, \dots$ such that $\{t_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\} = L$ (repetitions allowed, in arbitrary order); write $t[n] = (t_0, \dots, t_{n-1})$ and $\mathrm{content}(t[n]) = \{t_0, \dots, t_{n-1}\}$. A learner is a computable function $M$ mapping finite initial segments of texts to indices in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{?\}$. The learner $M$ converges on text $t$ to index $e$ if $M(t[n]) = e$ for all sufficiently large $n$. The family $\mathcal{L}$ is learnable from text by $M$ if, for every $i$ and every text $t$ for $L_i$, $M$ converges on $t$ to some index $e$ with $L_e = L_i$.

Define:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $M$ learns $\mathcal{L}$ with at most $k$ mind changes if, additionally, for every text $t$ for some $L_i$, the number of indices $n$ with $M(t[n]), M(t[n+1]) \in \mathbb{N}$ and $M(t[n]) \neq M(t[n+1])$ is at most $k$.
  \item $M$ learns $\mathcal{L}$ conservatively if, additionally, for every text $t$ for some $L_i$ and every $n$, whenever $M(t[n]) = e \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\mathrm{content}(t[n+1]) \subseteq L_e$, then $M(t[n+1]) = e$.
\end{itemize}

Question: Does there exist an indexed family $\mathcal{L}$ of recursive languages over $\mathbb{N}$ that is learnable from text with at most two mind changes but is not conservatively learnable from text?

Setup. Let $E$ be an ensemble of $n\times n$ real symmetric or complex Hermitian random matrices (for example a Wigner ensemble with i.i.d. entries of mean zero and finite variance). Let $A$ be a deterministic eigenvalue algorithm acting on Hermitian matrices that produces, starting from $M_0=M$ drawn from $E$, a sequence of isospectral iterates $M_0,M_1,M_2,\dots$ converging to a diagonal matrix (e.g. the Toda flow sampled at integer times, the QR algorithm, or the QR algorithm with shifts).

Halting (top‑gap) time. For $\varepsilon>0$, define the top‑gap halting time
$$\tau_{\varepsilon,n,A,E}(M)=\min\Bigl\{k\ge 0\ :\ \bigl|(M_k)_{n,n-1}\bigr|<\varepsilon\Bigr\},$$
which measures the first time the off‑diagonal entry coupling the last eigenvalue to the rest of the spectrum has dropped below $\varepsilon$.

Deflation time. Define the full deflation time
$$T_{\varepsilon,n,A,E}(M)=\min\Bigl\{k\ge 0\ :\ \max_{1\le j\le n-1}\bigl|(M_k)_{j+1,j}\bigr|<\varepsilon\Bigr\},$$
that is, the first iteration at which every sub‑diagonal entry of $M_k$ is smaller than $\varepsilon$, so that all eigenvalues have been numerically separated.

Known result (top‑gap universality). For $A$ equal to the Toda algorithm, there exist scaling constants $a_n=a_n(\varepsilon,A,E)$, $b_n=b_n(\varepsilon,A,E)$ and a distribution function $F_A$, independent of the choice of $E$ within a wide universality class, such that
$$\frac{\tau_{\varepsilon,n,A,E}-a_n}{b_n}\ \Longrightarrow\ F_A\qquad(n\to\infty).$$

Problem. Prove (or disprove) the analogous universality statement for the full deflation time: namely, exhibit an eigenvalue algorithm $A$ (e.g. Toda, QR, or QR with shifts), scaling constants $\widetilde a_n,\widetilde b_n$, and a distribution function $G_A$ such that
$$\frac{T_{\varepsilon,n,A,E}-\widetilde a_n}{\widetilde b_n}\ \Longrightarrow\ G_A\qquad(n\to\infty)$$
holds with $G_A$ independent of $E$ across an appropriate universality class (e.g. Wigner ensembles with sufficient moments). Unlike the top‑gap case, a proof must control not only the topmost spectral gap but also the joint behavior of all sub‑diagonal entries, equivalently the localization/delocalization and rigidity properties of the entire eigenvector basis throughout the iteration.

Rigorous universality has been established (Deift–Trogdon, 2016, and subsequent works including the recent monograph on the Toda lattice and universality) for the halting time associated with computing the largest eigenvalue (top eigen-gap) via the Toda algorithm, and analogous results for sample covariance matrices. Call a finite set X ⊂ ℝ^d a Ramsey set if for every positive integer r there exists an integer N such that for every N' ≥ N, every coloring of ℝ^{N'} with r colors contains a monochromatic congruent copy of X (i.e. an isometric image of X all of whose points receive the same color). For such a Ramsey set X and a positive integer r, define

  N(X, r) := the least integer N₀ such that for every N > N₀ and every r-coloring of ℝ^N, there is a monochromatic congruent copy of X.

Problem: For Ramsey sets X and integers r ≥ 2, determine or give good upper and lower bounds for N(X, r). In particular, treat the basic case in which X = {p, q} consists of two points at some fixed distance: determine the asymptotic behavior of N({p,q}, r) as a function of r (equivalently, determine how large the dimension N must be to guarantee that every r-coloring of ℝ^N contains two points at the prescribed distance receiving the same color).

Let m ≥ 2 be a fixed integer. A bivariate copula is a function C : [0,1]² → [0,1] such that C(x,0)=C(0,y)=0, C(x,1)=x, C(1,y)=y, and C is 2-increasing, i.e. for all 0 ≤ x₁ ≤ x₂ ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ y₁ ≤ y₂ ≤ 1,
   C(x₂,y₂) − C(x₂,y₁) − C(x₁,y₂) + C(x₁,y₁) ≥ 0.

For an integer k ≥ 1, points (x,y) ∈ [0,1]² and increments (u₁,v₁), …, (u_k,v_k) ∈ ℝ² such that for every subset J ⊆ {1,…,k} the point
   (x + Σ_{i∈J} u_i,  y + Σ_{i∈J} v_i)
lies in [0,1]², define the k-th alternating finite-difference of C at (x,y) with increments (u_i,v_i) by
   Δ_k C := Σ_{J ⊆ {1,…,k}} (−1)^{k+|J|} C(x + Σ_{i∈J} u_i,  y + Σ_{i∈J} v_i).

Call C m-ultramodular if Δ_k C ≥ 0 for every k ∈ {2,…,m} and every admissible choice of base point and increments as above.

A copula C is called associative if C(C(x,y),z) = C(x,C(y,z)) for all x,y,z ∈ [0,1]. An associative copula is Archimedean if it admits a representation
   C(x,y) = φ^{[-1]}(φ(x) + φ(y)),
where φ : [0,1] → [0,∞] is a continuous, strictly decreasing convex function with φ(1)=0, and φ^{[-1]} denotes the pseudo-inverse of φ.

Problem.
(a) Characterize the bivariate copulas C that are m-ultramodular.
(b) Characterize those m-ultramodular bivariate copulas which are associative.
(c) Characterize those m-ultramodular bivariate copulas which are Archimedean, and in particular characterize the additive generators φ of such copulas.

The case m=2 (ultramodular copulas) has been characterized: an ultramodular bivariate copula is exactly a 2-increasing copula whose horizontal and vertical sections are convex; sufficient conditions on additive generators of Archimedean ultramodular copulas are known and ultramodular copula constructions have been developed. Let $I=[0,1]$. A bivariate copula is a function $C:I^2\to I$ such that (i) $C(x,0)=C(0,x)=0$ and $C(x,1)=C(1,x)=x$ for all $x\in I$, and (ii) $C$ is 2-increasing, i.e. $C(x_2,y_2)-C(x_2,y_1)-C(x_1,y_2)+C(x_1,y_1)\ge 0$ for all $0\le x_1\le x_2\le 1$ and $0\le y_1\le y_2\le 1$. The diagonal section of $C$ is the function $\delta_C:I\to I$ defined by $\delta_C(x)=C(x,x)$.

Fix a point $x_0\in(0,1)$. Consider the class $\mathcal{C}_{x_0}$ of all bivariate copulas $C$ with the property that $C$ is affine (linear) on each segment joining the point $(x_0,x_0)$ to the corner $(1,0)$ and on each segment joining $(x_0,x_0)$ to the corner $(0,1)$, i.e. on the two families of line segments inside $I^2$ obtained by joining $(x_0,x_0)$ with points of the edges $\{(x,0):x\in I\}\cup\{(1,y):y\in I\}$ and $\{(0,y):y\in I\}\cup\{(x,1):x\in I\}$ that pass through $(x_0,x_0)$.

(a) Give a complete characterization of those functions $\delta:I\to I$ for which there exists $C\in\mathcal{C}_{x_0}$ with $\delta_C=\delta$.

(b) For each admissible diagonal $\delta$, determine whether there exist pointwise maximal and pointwise minimal copulas in the subclass $\{C\in\mathcal{C}_{x_0}:\delta_C=\delta\}$, and if so construct them explicitly.

Consider the class $\mathcal{C}_{x_0}$ of all bivariate copulas $C$ with the property that $C$ is affine (linear) on each segment joining the point $(x_0,x_0)$ to the corner $(1,0)$ and on each segment joining $(x_0,x_0)$ to the corner $(0,1)$, i.e. on the two families of line segments inside $I^2$ obtained by joining $(x_0,x_0)$ with points of the edges $\{(x,0):x\in I\}\cup\{(1,y):y\in I\}$ and $\{(0,y):y\in I\}\cup\{(x,1):x\in I\}$ that pass through $(x_0,x_0)$.

(a) Give a complete characterization of those functions $\delta:I\to I$ for which there exists $C\in\mathcal{C}_{x_0}$ with $\delta_C=\delta$.

(b) For each admissible diagonal $\delta$, determine whether there exist pointwise maximal and pointwise minimal copulas in the subclass $\{C\in\mathcal{C}_{x_0}:\delta_C=\delta\}$, and if so construct them explicitly.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

A follow-up work "A note on biconic copulas" (Kybernetika, 2011) explicitly studies the class of biconic copulas — those that are linear on segments joining a fixed diagonal point $(x_0,x_0)$ with the corners $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ — and proves a characterization theorem of admissible diagonal sections together with extreme constructions. Subsequent papers (e.g., on biconic aggregation functions with a given diagonal section, and on extreme semilinear copulas) extend and confirm this characterization, so the problem appears to be solved.

An abstract polytope of rank d (or d-polytope) is a partially ordered set P with a unique minimum element and a unique maximum element, in which every maximal chain (flag) has exactly d+2 elements, and which satisfies the usual diamond condition and strong flag-connectivity. Two flags are called adjacent if they differ in exactly one element. An automorphism of P is an order-preserving bijection P → P; the automorphism group Γ(P) acts on the set of flags.

The polytope P is called chiral if Γ(P) has exactly two orbits on the flags of P and any two adjacent flags lie in different orbits.

Problem. Determine precisely which finite non-abelian simple groups G arise as the automorphism group Γ(P) of some chiral d-polytope P, for some integer d ≥ 3.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The problem is partially solved. For rank d = 3 (chiral polyhedra), Leemans and Liebeck showed that every finite non-abelian simple group is the automorphism group of a chiral polyhedron, with the exceptions of PSL_2(q), PSL_3(q), PSU_3(q), and A_7. Subsequent work has addressed specific families (e.g., PSL(3,q), almost simple groups with socle PSL(2,q), and chiral 5-polytopes from alternating groups A_n by Conder–Hubard–O'Reilly Regueiro). The general classification across all ranks d remains an active area, with several recent papers (2022–2025), so the overall problem is not fully resolved.

A bivariate copula is a function $C:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ such that $C(u,0)=C(0,u)=0$, $C(u,1)=C(1,u)=u$ for all $u\in[0,1]$, and $C$ is 2-increasing, i.e. $C(u_2,v_2)-C(u_1,v_2)-C(u_2,v_1)+C(u_1,v_1)\ge 0$ for all $0\le u_1\le u_2\le 1$ and $0\le v_1\le v_2\le 1$. A copula $C$ is called associative if $C(C(u,v),w)=C(u,C(v,w))$ for all $u,v,w\in[0,1]$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ denote the set of all bivariate copulas equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on $[0,1]^2$, and let $\mathcal{C}_a\subseteq\mathcal{C}$ denote the set of associative bivariate copulas. Define $\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}_a$ as the closure (with respect to uniform convergence) of the convex hull of $\mathcal{C}_a$, i.e. the uniform closure of all finite convex combinations $\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i C_i$ with $C_i\in\mathcal{C}_a$, $\lambda_i\ge 0$, $\sum\lambda_i=1$.

(i) Characterize the extreme points of the convex set $\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}_a$ in the sense of the Krein–Milman theorem (a point $C\in\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}_a$ is extreme if $C=\tfrac{1}{2}(C_1+C_2)$ with $C_1,C_2\in\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}_a$ implies $C_1=C_2=C$).

(ii) Determine whether every extreme point of $\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}_a$ is also an extreme point of the full set $\mathcal{C}$ of bivariate copulas.

An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set P with a unique minimum element and unique maximum element, in which every maximal totally ordered subset (flag) has exactly n+2 elements (so elements naturally receive ranks 0,1,...,n-1 between the minimum and maximum), every flag has, for each i in {0,1,...,n-1}, a unique i-adjacent flag differing from it only in its rank-i element, P is strongly flag-connected, and P satisfies the diamond condition. For each i in {0,1,...,n-1}, let r_i be the permutation of the set of flags of P that sends every flag to its i-adjacent flag. Each r_i is an involution. The monodromy group (also called the connection group) of P is the subgroup Mon(P) = ⟨r_0, r_1, ..., r_{n-1}⟩ of the symmetric group on the flags.

A string C-group of rank n is a pair (G, {s_0,...,s_{n-1}}) where G is a group generated by involutions s_0,...,s_{n-1} satisfying:
 (1) (s_i s_j)^2 = 1 whenever |i-j| ≥ 2 (the string condition), and
 (2) the intersection property: for all subsets I, J ⊆ {0,...,n-1}, ⟨s_i : i ∈ I⟩ ∩ ⟨s_j : j ∈ J⟩ = ⟨s_k : k ∈ I ∩ J⟩.

Question: Does there exist a chiral abstract polytope P such that the monodromy group Mon(P), with its distinguished generating set {r_0, r_1, ..., r_{n-1}}, is not a string C-group?

Let n ≥ 2 and consider the unit hypercube [0,1]^n. An n-ary quasi-copula is a function Q : [0,1]^n → [0,1] satisfying:
(i) (Boundary conditions) Q(u_1,...,u_n) = 0 whenever at least one u_i = 0, and Q(1,...,1,u_i,1,...,1) = u_i for every i;
(ii) (Monotonicity) Q is nondecreasing in each variable;
(iii) (1-Lipschitz property) |Q(u) − Q(v)| ≤ Σ_{i=1}^n |u_i − v_i| for all u, v ∈ [0,1]^n.

For an n-dimensional Cartesian interval (box) I = [a_1,b_1] × ... × [a_n,b_n] ⊆ [0,1]^n, the Q-volume of I is
  V_Q(I) = Σ_{c} sgn(c) Q(c),
where the sum runs over the 2^n vertices c = (c_1,...,c_n) of I with c_i ∈ {a_i,b_i}, and sgn(c) = +1 if the number of i with c_i = a_i is even, and −1 otherwise.

Define the class F of "boundary-positive" n-ary quasi-copulas to be the set of all n-ary quasi-copulas Q such that V_Q(I) ≥ 0 for every n-dimensional box I ⊆ [0,1]^n that has at least one vertex on the topological boundary of [0,1]^n.

Problem: Give an intrinsic characterization of the class F. Moreover, identify and characterize natural distinguished subclasses of F (for example, classes obtained by restricting which boundary faces the vertex must lie on, or by additional regularity/structural conditions).

Determine the chromatic number $\chi(G)$, i.e., the least cardinal $\kappa$ such that there exists a function $c : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \kappa$ with $c(x) \neq c(y)$ whenever $\|x - y\|$ is an odd integer.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

Recent work (Davies, "Odd Distances in Colourings of the Plane", GAFA 2024) proved that every finite colouring of the plane contains a monochromatic pair of points at odd integer distance. Combined with the known existence of countable colourings of the odd-distance graph, this establishes that the chromatic number of the odd-distance graph in the plane equals $\aleph_0$, resolving Rosenfeld's problem.

representations.normalized:
An abstract polytope of rank $n$ is a partially ordered set $\mathcal{P}$, with a strictly monotone rank function onto $\{-1,0,1,\dots,n\}$, satisfying: (i) $\mathcal{P}$ has a unique minimum face (of rank $-1$) and a unique maximum face (of rank $n$); (ii) every maximal chain (flag) has exactly $n+2$ elements; (iii) $\mathcal{P}$ is strongly flag-connected; and (iv) the diamond condition: whenever $F < G$ with $\mathrm{rank}(G)-\mathrm{rank}(F)=2$, there are exactly two faces strictly between $F$ and $G$. An automorphism of $\mathcal{P}$ is an order-preserving bijection. The polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is called regular if its automorphism group acts transitively on flags, and chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags such that adjacent flags lie in different orbits.

Given two abstract polytopes $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ of the same rank, $\mathcal{P}$ is said to cover $\mathcal{Q}$ if there exists a surjection $\mathcal{P} \to \mathcal{Q}$ which preserves rank, incidence, and adjacency of flags; one then says $\mathcal{Q}$ is a quotient of $\mathcal{P}$. For regular polytopes, there is a well-developed theory in which quotients correspond to certain normal subgroups of the automorphism group of the universal regular polytope of a given Schläfli type.

Develop the analogous theory of covers and quotients in the chiral setting. Specifically:
(a) Formulate the appropriate notions of "chiral cover" and "chiral quotient" between chiral polytopes (and possibly between chiral and regular polytopes), accounting for the role of the two flag orbits and the handedness (mirror image) of chiral polytopes.
(b) Give a group-theoretic characterization of chiral covers in terms of the rotation subgroups (or their analogues) of the automorphism groups, identifying which subgroups give rise to chiral quotients that are again polytopes.
(c) Establish the analogue, in the chiral setting, of the regular-cover theory: in particular, describe a universal chiral polytope of a prescribed Schläfli type from which all chiral polytopes of that type arise as quotients, and characterize the corresponding covering relations.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Partial progress has been made on aspects of chiral covers since the problem was posed. Notable contributions include work on abelian covers of chiral polytopes (Cunningham–Pellicer, J. Algebra 2017), chiral extensions of chiral polytopes (Cunningham–Pellicer), and the study of chiral polytopes whose smallest regular cover is itself a polytope (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A, 2024). However, a complete general theory of chiral covers and quotients fully analogous to the regular-cover theory does not appear to have been established in the literature, so the program as a whole remains open.
